# Izzet Prowess

- **Format:** Casual 60-card, 1v1
- **Archetype:** Izzet Prowess / spells-tempo: cheap creatures that grow or deal damage whenever you cast a spell, 10 cheap burn spells, cantrips and a few counterspells
- **Played by:** either. Suits whoever enjoys tricks, timing and counting damage. It rewards careful play more than Gruul does.
- **Status:** idea
- **Paired against:** [Gruul Ramp](gruul-ramp.md)
- **Complexity:** 3/5
- **Estimated power:** 5.5 with owned cards only, 6.5 with the buys (on a 1v1 scale)
- **Configuration:** Pair 2. It uses no precon cards, so its cards have all arrived and it can be built now. It's in **both** the Now set and the Commander-season set, so it never has to be taken apart.

A fast blue-red spells deck. Its creatures get bigger, or deal damage, every time you cast an instant or sorcery. Ten cheap burn spells kill Gruul's mana creatures early, and a few counterspells and 'turn it into a 1/1' spells handle its giants. You win by flying over the top and burning Gruul out before its big creatures take over. It suits a player who enjoys tricks, timing and working out damage.

### Why these buys (in priority order)

1. **3x Sprite Dragon** (replaces 2 Firespitter Whelp + 1 Enigma Drake). A 2-mana flying, hasty threat that gets a permanent +1/+1 counter every time you cast a noncreature spell. It's a Dragon, so the upgraded Gruul's Glorybringer can't target it with its exert ability. In the matchup simulator it was the best-value threat for this deck (+3.6 to +3.7 percentage points). No reprint is announced. *Also useful in: Bria, Riptide Rogue Commander (in about 26% of Bria decks on EDHREC)..*
2. **4x Sulfur Falls** (replaces 4 Swiftwater Cliffs). A U/R dual land that enters untapped when you control an Island or Mountain, so 1–2 drops come down on curve and you can hold up Counterspell. It was the single biggest gain in the matchup simulator (+4 points). Reprinted in Reality Fracture Commander (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices, so there's no need to wait. *Also useful in: Bria Commander (in about 73% of Bria decks on EDHREC) or any U/R deck.*
3. **2x Electrolyze** (replaces 2 Think Twice). Deals 2 damage divided between one or two targets, then draws a card. It kills two mana elves (or an elf plus 1 to the face) and replaces itself: simple card advantage aimed at Gruul's ramp. Cast on your own turn, its draw is your second card that turn, so Mischievous Mystic also makes a Faerie. It's a small upgrade (+0.7 points), chosen on purpose to keep the target pair even. *Also useful in: Any U/R deck, including a Bria Commander build (not an EDHREC top card for Bria)..*

### Shared-pool conflicts

Shares no physical cards with any other deck: [Mono-White Angels](mono-white-angels.md), [Mono-Black Zombies](mono-black-zombies.md), [Gruul Ramp](gruul-ramp.md), [Selesnya Rabbits](selesnya-rabbits.md), [Orzhov Vampires](orzhov-vampires.md), [Mono-Black Midrange](mono-black-midrange.md), [Orzhov Removal Midrange](orzhov-removal.md), [Giada, Font of Hope: Calling All Angels (upgraded)](../commander/giada-angels.md), [Ghoulcaller Gisa: Wretched Ranks (upgraded)](../commander/gisa-zombies.md), [Finneas, Ace Archer: Rabbits, Tokens and Counters](../commander/finneas-rabbits.md).

## Substitutes

| Buy (target list) | Play until it arrives (owned list) | What the swap costs |
|---|---|---|
| 4 Sulfur Falls | 4 Swiftwater Cliffs | Cliffs always enter tapped, so about one game in three you can't cast your 2-drop on time or keep Counterspell open. It's the biggest loss (about 4 points of win rate in testing), partly offset by the 1 life each Cliffs gains. |
| 3 Sprite Dragon | 2 Firespitter Whelp + 1 Enigma Drake | Both cost 3 instead of 2 and don't grow permanently; Drake's power equals the instants and sorceries in your graveyard. Whelp does ping for 1 per noncreature spell. About 3–4 points weaker. |
| 2 Electrolyze | 2 Think Twice | Think Twice draws cards (and its flashback is a second draw on Gruul's turn for Mystic) but can't kill mana elves. About 1 point weaker. |

## Notes

**Game plan.** You're the fast, tricky deck. Play cheap creatures on turns 1–3, then cast lots of cheap spells.
- *Prowess* means "whenever you cast a spell that isn't a creature, this creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn".
- Coruscation Mage and Firespitter Whelp deal 1 damage to Gruul whenever you cast a noncreature spell (Whelp also when you cast a Dragon, such as Sprite Dragon). Guttersnipe deals 2 whenever you cast an instant or sorcery.
- Early on, aim burn (Burst Lightning, Lightning Bolt, Abrade, Scorching Dragonfire, Electrolyze) at Gruul's mana creatures (Llanowar Elves, Druid of the Cowl, Ruby) and helpers (Halana and Alena, Scavenging Ooze). That makes their giants arrive late.
- **Don't burn Sakura-Tribe Elder.** Gruul just sacrifices it in response to fetch its land, and your spell does nothing.
- One burn spell won't kill a giant (5/5 and bigger). A kicked Burst Lightning (4 damage) does kill 4-toughness creatures (Tajuru Pathwarden, Surrak, Gnarlback Rhino, Glorybringer). In an emergency, two burn spells on the same 5/5 (Bolt plus Burst or Abrade) kill it.
- Otherwise answer giants with Counterspell, Essence Scatter, Witness Protection (turns a creature into a 1/1 with no abilities), Charmed Sleep (it stays tapped) or Into the Roil (back to their hand).
- Witness Protection and Charmed Sleep are Auras, so cast them on your own turn, not in response.
- Charmed Sleep only stops attacking and blocking; the creature's other abilities keep working. Put it on plain beaters (Quakestrider Ceratops, Pelakka Wurm, Terror of Mount Velus, Quaketusk Boar). Save Witness Protection for creatures whose abilities matter (Rampaging Baloths, Aggressive Mammoth, Lathliss, Halana and Alena).
- Win in the air with Mischievous Mystic and Sprite Dragon (or Whelp and Enigma Drake in the owned list), with pings, and with burn to the face.
- Mischievous Mystic makes a 1/1 flying Faerie whenever you draw your second card in a turn. On your own turn, any Preordain, Think Twice or Electrolyze does it, because your draw step was the first card.
- Tolarian Terror costs 1 less for every instant and sorcery in your graveyard, so by turn 5 it's often a 5/5 for 2–3 mana.

**Opening hand and mulligan.**
- Keep 7 cards if you have 2–4 lands, at least one blue and one red source (dual lands count), and something to do on turns 1–2: a cheap creature, burn or Preordain.
- To mulligan, shuffle, draw a new 7, then put 1 card on the bottom for each mulligan you've taken.
- Mulligan 7-card hands with 0–1 lands or 5+ lands, and hands missing a colour entirely (unless you hold Preordain).
- After one mulligan, keep anything with 2–4 lands.

**Play tips.**
1. **Kill the first mana creature.** A turn-1 Llanowar Elves lets Gruul cast a 5/5 on turn 3, so on your turn 2, spending Burst Lightning or Bolt on it is almost always better than casting a 2-drop.
2. **Cast spells after blocks.** Attack first. If Gruul blocks a prowess creature, then cast Preordain or a burn spell to make it bigger and win the fight. If they don't block, those spells add extra damage.
3. **Hold up Counterspell.** From about turn 4, keep two blue mana (UU) open during Gruul's turn. Save it for the big threats (Rampaging Baloths, Aggressive Mammoth, Quakestrider Ceratops, Lathliss, Terror of Mount Velus, Pelakka Wurm, and later Glorybringer and Thragtusk), not for elves. When Fierce Empath resolves, their biggest creature is coming next.
4. **Heartfire Immolator.** Pay R and sacrifice it to deal damage equal to its power to a creature. Pump it with spells first, or do it in response when Gruul tries to kill it.
5. **Stormcatch Mentor** makes instants and sorceries cost 1 less, but only the generic part: Bolt and Burst still cost R, and Abrade drops to R.
6. **Don't swing with everything when you're low.** Gruul's creatures often have trample (Garruk's Uprising, Aggressive Mammoth, Quaketusk Boar, Baloths), so small chump blockers barely help. Keep enough back, or make sure your attack wins.
7. **Count to 20.** Once Gruul is on about 8 life or less, aim burn at their face; every spell also triggers your pingers. The deck is stronger going first (about 55% on the play and 47% on the draw in testing), so take turns at who plays first.

**Watch out for (Gruul).**
- Snakeskin Veil (owned list only): for G, their creature gets hexproof and a +1/+1 counter, so your spell, or Heartfire's ability, fizzles. Burn it when they're tapped out.
- Garruk's Uprising gives their team trample, and draws them a card whenever a creature with power 4 or more enters.
- Rampaging Baloths makes a 4/4 whenever a land enters under their control, including lands from Sakura-Tribe Elder or Clifftop Lookout. Answer it at once, preferably with a counter or Witness Protection.
- Halana and Alena grows another creature and gives it haste every turn. Kill it on sight; it also has first strike and reach, so it blocks your fliers.
- Terror of Mount Velus is a flying double striker: 10 damage a hit. The turn it enters, their whole team gets double strike.
- Bite Down and Rabid Gnaw let their big creature hit yours at instant speed.
- Wildheart Invoker: late game, {8} gives one attacker +5/+5 and trample.
- In the upgraded Gruul:
  - Glorybringer: flying and haste. When it attacks it can exert to deal 4 damage to one of your non-Dragon creatures, then it skips its next untap. Sprite Dragon and Firespitter Whelp are Dragons, so they're safe.
  - Thragtusk: gains 5 life and leaves a 3/3 behind even when bounced, so don't waste Into the Roil on it.

**Sideboard: only against stronger opponents, never against Gruul.**
- Against creature-heavy decks: bring in Blasphemous Act, Voracious Greatshark and Charmed Sleep #2. Take out 2 Think Twice/Electrolyze and 1 Mischievous Mystic.
  - Blasphemous Act costs 1 less for each creature on the battlefield and deals 13 to every creature. Cast it when they have more creatures than you.
  - It's kept out of the main deck because it's a near one-sided wipe against Gruul.
- Against spell-heavy or control decks: bring in Negate and 2 Spell Pierce. Take out Essence Scatter, Witness Protection and Charmed Sleep.

### Head-to-head vs Gruul Ramp (tested)

**Verdict: even**, about 51/49 Izzet with competent play on both sides. If the Izzet player is still learning, it's closer to 49/51.

| Izzet win % | Original simulator | Re-checked simulator |
|---|---|---|
| Owned vs owned | 51–53% | 51% (49% with beginner-level Izzet play) |
| Both with buys | 51–53% | 51% (49% with beginner-level Izzet play) |
| Izzet with buys, Gruul owned | 60% | 59% |
| Izzet owned, Gruul with buys | 41% | 42% |

**How it was tested.** A rules simulator played 32,000 games per matchup, alternating who goes first. An independent re-check found a bug worth about 2 points to Izzet (Gruul never sacrificed Sakura-Tribe Elder in response to burn) and five smaller gaps. It fixed them all, then restored the balance with one list change: Gruul's Obliterating Bolt moved to the sideboard and Wildheart Invoker came in. Twelve simulator games were also reviewed turn by turn (6–6), and 8 more were played by hand. Gruul won 6 of those 8, but the simulator also favoured Gruul on the same deals (Izzet won 41%).

**Going first is the biggest single factor.** Izzet wins about 55% on the play and 47% on the draw. Take turns going first, or let Izzet start if Gruul keeps winning.

#### Why it's even
- The red cards are split. Izzet has all the cheap burn and the prowess creatures. Gruul has the big burn, the bite spells and the red giants.
- Izzet's burn kills Gruul's mana creatures but not its giants. For those it has counterspells, Witness Protection, Charmed Sleep, Into the Roil, kicked Burst Lightning and double burn. Gruul's 7 main-deck removal spells kill any Izzet creature except Tolarian Terror.
- **Gruul wins** when a mana creature survives or it lands a 6-drop that Izzet can't answer. **Izzet wins** when it kills the early elves and races with flyers and pings. Izzet's results depend more on how well it's played.

#### Buying rule
Izzet's buys are worth about +8 points and Gruul's about +9, so upgrade both decks together. Otherwise buy the threats first for both (Sprite Dragon ×3 with Glorybringer ×2, tested at 51%), not the lands first (about 53% Izzet). On 2026-09-28 MTGMate had no Glorybringer or Electrolyze, so find those at Good Games or the local shop. Keep both decks on their owned lists until both packages are complete, then swap them in on the same day.

#### Tuning levers (measured in the re-checked simulator)
- **If Gruul wins too often:** let Izzet go first (see above). Card swaps help Izzet only a little: Gruul's Fiery Annihilation → Beast-Kin Ranger is +0.3 to +0.7 for Izzet.
- **If Izzet wins too often:** Gruul's Wildheart Invoker → Obliterating Bolt from its sideboard (−2 to −3 for Izzet), or Gruul's Fierce Empath → Giant Cindermaw (about −1.5).
- **If Izzet feels too complicated:** cut to 1 Counterspell and add Opt (about −0.6 for Izzet), and let Izzet go first.
- **Not levers:** Izzet's Mischievous Mystic → Charmed Sleep (−0.6 for Izzet, the wrong direction). Gruul's Garruk's Uprising → Harmonize won't work either: Harmonize is in the Selesnya Rabbits sideboard, so both decks couldn't be built in the Commander-season set.
- Most single-card swaps move the result by less than 1 point, so log about 10 real games before changing anything.

Simulator code and full game logs from the 2026-09-28 analysis are not kept in the repo.
